# ggez-scoped dirs-sys patch

This directory contains selected files from published `dirs-sys` 0.5.0, Cargo registry checksum `e01a3366d27ee9890022452ee61b2b63a67e6f13f58900b651ff5665f0bb1fab`, upstream revision `8bcd4aa2c35990d57a2cff2953793525fc42709c`. The upstream MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses are retained. `Cargo.toml.orig` and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` are historical upstream provenance, not the active modified manifest. The retained upstream README has one trailing-whitespace cleanup.

The active Cargo manifest removes `option-ext`; `src/lib.rs` removes its extern declaration. In the Unix XDG user-directory parser, the only `OptionExt` call is replaced with the standard `Option<&str> == Some(key)` comparison. A Unix-only regression exercises unspecified, matching, and nonmatching requested keys. The Windows implementation and its known-folder calls are unchanged. Only `experiments/ggez` selects this patch; other experiments retain their own locked dependencies. Updating the lock also changed the `windows-sys` selection for `errno`, `rustix` and `winapi-util` from 0.61.2 to 0.52.0, while retaining their package versions. Those resolver changes require cross-platform review alongside the patch.

The XDG parser test must be run on a Unix host; Windows cannot compile or exercise that Unix-only module. This patch removes the identified crate from this ggez graph, not all possible MPL, LGPL or GPLv3 content from source, native libraries, assets, toolchains or system dependencies. See `docs/packaging/GGEZ-WINDOWS-OPTION-EXT-PATCH.md` for bounded platform validation.
